correctness.rationale: For each ordered composition, the total valuation equals the sum of binary carries, including carry sizes. All terms with valuation zero contribute 1 modulo 8, exactly-one-carry terms contribute 4, and larger valuation terms vanish; disjoint exact counts yield formula (1). For even \(h\ge4\) all even coefficients vanish modulo 8. The Lucas parity of \(\binom{\ell}{2}\), \(\binom{\ell}{3}\) supplies (3)-(4); independent high-bit parity gives exact \(2^{k-2}\) occurrences in all four odd residues. Boundary cases \(\ell=1\), \(n=0\), \(k=2\) are explicit. The exact embedded verifier checks four heights 2..8, 32 levels and \(n\le512\), with factorial enumeration and single-carry counts; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim gives the all-level all-index one-carry congruence modulo eight and sharp height threshold, and exact four-residue dyadic counts for odd levels 3 modulo 4. Sun 2607.07638 supplies definitions and different weighted prime congruences; Beluhov 2506.12789 supplies significant pre-existing valuations, not equivalent residues and dyadic distribution. Queries on exact \(S_{\ell}^{(2)}\), Abelian squares, equivalent carry formulations, generalized Domb sums and modulo eight did not identify a stronger covering result; absence of an indexed hit alone is not proof of novelty. The known central-binomial and Domb slices are explicitly not treated as original.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent formula may exist under Abelian-square enumeration or finite automaton language in unindexed literature.
For level two and four, earlier work supplies stronger numerical/divisibility facts, so the claim of novelty concerns the uniform statement and exact odd-level residue census.
An exhaustive search of every OEIS comment, publisher appendix and subsequent preprint has not been performed; absence of search hits is not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The published multinomial-power family has natural level/height parameters with Franel, Domb and Abelian-square interpretations. The modulus 8 is mathematically distinguished as the first one where exactly one binary carry survives after squaring, providing a universal termwise digital characterization. Unlike a numerical table or isolated special case, the theorem derives an exact four-way dyadic equidistribution for all levels \(\ell\equiv3\pmod4\) and a sparse-support phenomenon for even levels, with a sharp transition between height 2 and even heights \(h\ge4\).
